title: I have RM1 million to invest in property. How would Sean structure it?
videoTitle: ASKING SEAN #222 | WITH RM 1MIL BUDGET, WHAT WOULD I DO?
excerpt: A 30-year-old returning to Sabah with RM1 million to RM1.5 million asks how many properties to buy and where to find them. Sean says skip the count, learn the buying channels and never buy above median.

qa.asker: D, a viewer who wrote in by email
qa.context: D is 30, married with a baby due in 2024, and is returning from working overseas to live in Sabah, where his home is sorted. He has about RM1 million to invest in property, up to RM1.5 million if needed, a share portfolio yielding about 5%, no debts and will earn about RM10,000 a month. He finds Sabah prices high against local incomes and is open to buying in West Malaysia, landed or high-rise, aiming for rent that covers 80% of the repayment.
qa.question: How many properties should he aim for, where and how should he source them, and how should he rent and manage them?
qa.quote: The goal is to buy money making properties.
qa.answer: Don't aim for a number of properties: three good ones beat six weak ones. Before buying anything, visit about 20 properties across types, areas and both sides of Malaysia, learn the four ways to buy, and never pay above the median price. Keep the money in shares meanwhile; property prices won't run away in a year.

reasons.title: Counting properties leads to bad buys
reasons.body: Chasing a target makes it tempting to add small, weak units just to raise the count. Adding a property feels good, like a new pair of shoes, but the aim is income and wealth.

reasons.title: Where you buy changes the price you pay
reasons.body: Buying from a developer usually means the full retail price; a subsale gives certainty and room to negotiate; auctions often end near market price and can hide caveats and unpaid maintenance; bulk purchases can unlock deals individuals never see.

reasons.title: Local markets behave differently
reasons.body: Sabah and Sarawak don't see Kuala Lumpur's flood of launches, and some landed homes in Kota Kinabalu and Kuching have grown well, so oversupply isn't a nationwide fact. Living in Sabah gives him local knowledge worth using.

reasons.title: His income sets the pace
reasons.body: Cash isn't his limit; a RM10,000 salary is, perhaps RM3,000 to RM4,000 a month for instalments. Buying one property at a time and declaring its rent as income keeps his debt service ratio healthy for the next.

actions: Visit about 20 properties of different types and areas, in Sabah and West Malaysia, before buying.
Compare developer, subsale, auction and bulk purchase prices for the same kind of unit.
Check the median price in each area and don't buy above it.
Buy one at a time, let the first unit's rent show in your income records, then buy the next.
Consider your wife's name and loan eligibility for a later purchase.
qa.caveat: Sean wouldn't name specific projects: the same unit can cost different buyers different prices depending on their access to deals. His bulk purchase suggestion comes from a group he is a customer of.

sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's full English captions for Asking Sean #222. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased. Figures are as the viewer stated them in September 2023. Sean says he is a customer of the bulk purchase group he recommends.
